question: Which products send the most people to the ER in 2025?
response:
Based on the 2025 NEISS emergency department data, here are the top products/consumer environments sending the most people to the ER (ranked by estimated national injury totals using NEISS statistical weights):

1. **Floors or flooring materials** (Code 1807): ~2,199,378 estimated injuries (47,267 reported cases)
2. **Stairs or steps** (Code 1842): ~1,228,377 estimated injuries (29,531 reported cases)
3. **Beds or bedframes** (Code 4076): ~999,656 estimated injuries (25,989 reported cases)
4. **Chairs, other or not specified** (Code 4074): ~433,183 estimated injuries (10,818 reported cases)
5. **Bicycles or accessories** (Code 5040): ~412,756 estimated injuries (10,456 reported cases)
6. **Bathtubs or showers** (Code 611): ~369,916 estimated injuries (8,647 reported cases)
7. **Exercise (activity/apparel without equipment)** (Code 3299): ~361,889 estimated injuries (8,476 reported cases)
8. **Basketball** (Code 1205): ~358,220 estimated injuries (10,306 reported cases)
9. **Knives, not elsewhere classified** (Code 464): ~342,503 estimated injuries (7,034 reported cases)
10. **Football** (Code 1211): ~307,911 estimated injuries (9,754 reported cases)

*(Note: NEISS tracks injuries associated with structural building materials and common household items alongside traditional consumer products).*

tool_calls.name: run_sql

args.query:
SELECT 
    n.product_code, 
    p.title AS product_name, 
    COUNT(*) AS er_visits,
    ROUND(SUM(n.weight), 1) AS estimated_total_injuries
FROM neiss n
LEFT JOIN product_codes p ON n.product_code = p.code
WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(n.treatment_date AS DATE)) = 2025
GROUP BY n.product_code, p.title
ORDER BY estimated_total_injuries DESC
LIMIT 15;
